title: Maximum Total Damage With Spell Casting
pattern: DP on Sorted Unique Values with Two Pointers
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<long long> vals: up to n entries → O(n)
- vector<long long> cnt: up to n entries → O(n)
- vector<long long> dp: up to n+1 entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- sort(): O(log n) stack
- not counted: input (modified in place), returned scalar
approach: Sort the spells and group identical damage values together (hint 1: if we use power x, use all of them). Let `vals[]` be the sorted unique damages and `cnt[]` their frequencies. Use DP where `dp[i+1]` = max damage using the first `i+1` unique values: either skip value `i` (`dp[i]`) or take all spells of value `vals[i]` plus the best solution using only values `<= vals[i]-3` (since `vals[i]-2, vals[i]-1, vals[i]+1, vals[i]+2` are forbidden, and values are sorted/distinct so only the lower side matters). A two-pointer `ptr` tracks how many unique values are `<= vals[i]-3`, giving O(n log n) total.
hints: If you decide to cast even one spell of damage x, is there any reason not to cast every other spell with that same damage x?
Dynamic programming on sorted unique damage values. For power = [1,1,3,4], group into (1→2, 3→3, 4→4); at value 4, the best compatible predecessor is value 1 (since 4−3=1), giving 2+4=6.

```
sort and group by damage value → vals[], sums[]
dp[0] = sums[0]
ptr = -1
for i = 1 to m-1:
    while ptr+1 < i and vals[ptr+1] <= vals[i] - 3:
        ptr++
    take = sums[i] + (ptr >= 0 ? dp[ptr] : 0)
    dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], take)
return dp[m-1]
```

**Single spell** - only one element in the array
`Input: power = [5]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: not initializing dp[0] when m==1 → returns 0

**All duplicates** - every spell has the same damage value
`Input: power = [3,3,3]` → `Expected: 9`
⚠️ Bug: counting each unique value once instead of summing all occurrences → returns 3

**Consecutive values** - all values within 2 of each other, so at most one group can be chosen
`Input: power = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: using vals[i] - 2 instead of vals[i] - 3 in the compatibility check → returns 4

**Overflow** - three spells with damage 10^9, sum = 3×10^9 exceeds 2^31−1
`Input: power = [1000000000, 1000000000, 1000000000]` → `Expected: 3000000000`
⚠️ Bug: using int for sums → 3000000000 overflows to -1294967296

followUps.q: What if the forbidden range was [x−k, x+k] for a general k instead of [x−2, x+2]?
followUps.a: Replace the condition vals[i] - 3 with vals[i] - k - 1 in the two-pointer. Everything else stays the same. Time complexity remains O(n log n), space O(n).

followUps.q: What if we also need to output which spells to cast, not just the maximum damage?
followUps.a: Store a backpointer array: for each i, record whether we took or skipped, and if taken, which j we used. Backtrack from dp[m-1] to reconstruct the chosen damage values, then map back to original spell indices. Time stays O(n log n), space increases by O(n) for backpointers (already O(n) total).

followUps.q: What if power[i] could be negative?
followUps.a: Add a base case allowing zero spells: initialize dp[i] = max(dp[i], 0
